theory.intro: A quadrilateral is a four-sided shape. It is named by its sides and angles: equal sides (tick marks), right angles (small square) and parallel sides (arrows).
facts: **Rectangle**: opposite sides equal and $4$ right angles.
**Rhombus**: $4$ equal sides, opposite sides parallel (no right angles needed).
steps: Check for right angles (small square marks).
Check which sides are equal (tick marks) and which are parallel (arrows).
Match the properties to the most specific name.

foundation.solution_text:
All four sides carry the same single tick, and every corner is marked as a right angle.
Square

Opposite sides carry matching ticks and every corner is a right angle, but adjacent sides are not equal.
Rectangle

All four sides carry the same single tick and both pairs of opposite sides are marked parallel, with no right angle.
Rhombus

Both pairs of opposite sides are marked parallel and equal, but adjacent sides are not equal and there is no right angle.
Parallelogram

Only one pair of opposite sides carries the parallel arrows, and no sides are marked equal.
Trapezium

There are two pairs of equal sides, and each pair sits next to each other rather than opposite each other.
Kite

Reading clockwise from $W$ gives $W$, then $X$, then $Y$, then $Z$.
$WXYZ$

foundation.question_text: A quadrilateral has four equal sides and four right angles. Name it.
foundation.solution_text:
Only one special quadrilateral has both four equal sides and four right angles.
Square

foundation.question_text: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. Name it.
foundation.solution_text:
A parallelogram needs two pairs of parallel sides, so one pair only rules it out.
Trapezium

development.solution_text:
Turning the page does not change the marks: four equal sides and four right angles.
Square

The lengths give two pairs of equal opposite sides, $5$ cm and $3$ cm, and every corner is a right angle.
Rectangle

Two right angles are marked, but only one pair of sides carries the parallel arrows, so it is not a rectangle.
Trapezium

development.question_text: Which property does every rectangle have that a parallelogram need not have?
development.solution_text:
Both have opposite sides equal and parallel.
Only the rectangle must have all four angles equal to $90^{\circ}$.

development.question_text: Which property does every rhombus have that a rectangle need not have?
development.solution_text:
Both have opposite sides parallel.
Only the rhombus must have all four sides equal.

development.question_text: State the two properties of the sides of a parallelogram that are always true.
development.solution_text:
Opposite sides are parallel.
Opposite sides are equal in length.

Vertices must be read in order around the shape, either clockwise or anticlockwise.
Reading around Tommy’s sketch gives $ABDC$, not $ABCD$.
Swapping the labels $C$ and $D$ makes it rectangle $ABCD$.

development.question_text: A quadrilateral has two pairs of equal sides, the equal sides are next to each other, and no sides are parallel. Name it.
development.solution_text:
Equal sides that sit next to each other are adjacent, not opposite, and no pair is parallel.
Kite

development.question_text: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides and exactly one pair of equal angles. Explain why it cannot be a kite.
development.solution_text:
A kite has no pair of parallel sides at all.
The parallel pair rules a kite out, so the quadrilateral is a trapezium.

mastery.question_text: A quadrilateral has four equal angles. Its opposite sides are equal, but its adjacent sides are not. Name it, and state the one change to its sides that would make it a square.
mastery.solution_text:
Four equal angles in a quadrilateral are four right angles, and the opposite sides are equal.
Rectangle
Making all four sides equal would make it a square.

mastery.question_text: Ali says that any quadrilateral with two pairs of equal sides must be a parallelogram. Name a special quadrilateral that shows Ali is wrong, and describe how its equal sides are arranged.
mastery.solution_text:
A parallelogram has its two pairs of equal sides opposite each other.
A kite also has two pairs of equal sides, but they are adjacent — each pair meets at a vertex.
A kite shows Ali is wrong.

mastery.question_text: In quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AB$ is parallel to $DC$, $AB = 6$ cm, $DC = 10$ cm and $\angle ADC = 90^{\circ}$. Name the most specific special quadrilateral that $ABCD$ must be, and give the reason.
mastery.solution_text:
If both pairs of opposite sides were parallel, $AB$ and $DC$ would be equal.
$AB = 6$ cm and $DC = 10$ cm are unequal, so only one pair of sides is parallel.
Trapezium
